undated_mentions: First trip to Spain at age eight
First public singing with Hotel Aveneda orchestra in Madrid (age eight)
First English poems inspired by On the Waterfront (age nine)
Silver medal in a Spanish Juvenile Art Contest (early years)
Performed at school-end party with a trio (age 15)
Wrote screenplays and science-fiction short stories (1960s and 1970s)
Spent over a year in France after military service, working in film
Translator and second assistant to Joseph L. Mankiewicz on Cleopatra
Ed Ames recorded Aleluya #1 as Who Will Answer, a US hit
Created soundtracks for films by Chávarri, Berlanga, Fernán-Gómez, Méndez (by the 1970s)
Designed album covers during a break from music
Hospitalised with tuberculosis in Cuba for five months after 1977 festival invitation
Shared a concert stage with Silvio Rodríguez (Mano a Mano)
Ad Libidum exhibit tour in Latin America and Spain (mid 1990s)
Retrospective of his work in Zaragoza (after 2010)
